sent_to_model:
I did my last ever night shift on Saturday. After 14 years of nights I have finally been moved onto the days-only rota, and I am surprisingly not okay about it. I keep wanting to write something for the blog, the one I've neglected since spring, but every time I sit down it turns into either a eulogy or a complaint about the NHS, and I don't want either. I want it to be honest about what nights gave me and what they took. A few of my regulars read it, some colleagues, my sister in Bangalore. Can you help me draft it? It can be sad in places but please don't make it maudlin, and no patient should be identifiable.

- last night shift Sat 7 Nov 2026, 21:00 to 07:30, majors. 14 years of nights total, first one as an SHO in 2012
- moving to days-only rota from Monday, partly my knees and sleep, partly the GP said my blood pressure is not a joke anymore
- our charge nurse on nights, Folasade, has done nights for 22 years and still beats me up the stairs
- the 4am toast. someone always makes toast in the staff room at 4. nobody admits to starting it
- first winter of nights I cried in the car park at the Infirmary because I couldn't remember if I had given the second dose. I had. Still remember the frost on the windscreen
- an old gentleman last winter, around 3am, held my hand and told me I had his daughter's hands. he went home three days later. (keep vague, no details)
- drove home Sunday morning down the London Road, sun coming up, Radio 4 shipping forecast on catch-up, and realised I would not see that light from this side again
- missed both my nieces' naming ceremonies over video because of nights, my sister never once complained
- nights are where the department is most itself. fewer managers, more honesty, more kindness
- people think nights are about adrenaline but mostly it is about staying kind at 5am when you are empty
- I'm relieved and I feel like a traitor for being relieved
- not a complaint about staffing, I've written enough of those
- end somewhere hopeful-ish, maybe about the toast or about Folasade, not about me

(About me: emergency-medicine doctor, 42, Leicester, England. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

must_cover: Reflects on what fourteen years of night shifts gave the doctor and what they cost.
Explains the mixed feelings about moving to days.
Ends somewhere hopeful, without centring the ending on the doctor.
Keeps the reflection from becoming a complaint about the NHS or staffing.
must_not_reveal: Information that could identify any patient.
Additional clinical or personal details about the elderly gentleman beyond the vague anecdote supplied.
